A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thickened cell walls of B. cereus grown in chloramphenicol are unstable and can be easily degraded.
the thickened wall fragments are not simply "shed" from the cell surface.
chloramphenicol-induced thickened cell walls are not stable and they are gradually removed from the surface of growing cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thickened cell walls of chlorampheni-col-treated B. cereus are not stable structures, but rather are dynamic and are shed from the surface of the cell during cell growth.
the thickened wall fragments are shed off during the cell cycle, and the thickened wall material is not transferred to daughter cells.
the thickened wall is not a rigid structure but a fragile one, and the thickening process may not be a simple one but a complex and dynamic process.
